headline: EU CSRD Assurance Drafts Published Alongside Ecodesign Repairability Consultation
summary: The European Commission has published draft sustainability reporting assurance standards under CSRD, impacting your upcoming FY2027 reporting obligations. Meanwhile, consultations have opened on ESPR repairability rules relevant to power and garden tools, and reports indicate the Green Claims Directive may be abandoned.

items.title: Draft Sustainability Reporting Assurance Standards Published Under CSRD
items.what: The European Commission published draft standards for the mandatory assurance of corporate sustainability reporting under CSRD.
items.meaning: As a listed entity in scope for FY2027 reporting under Omnibus I rules, your sustainability disclosures will require independent assurance, including data collected from Chinese suppliers.
items.action: Review draft assurance criteria against your current supplier ESG data collection processes.

sources.title: EU Commission Releases Draft Sustainability Reporting Assurance Standards

items.title: EU Opens Consultation on Ecodesign Repairability Requirements
items.what: The European Commission launched a consultation regarding repairability requirements under ecodesign rules.
items.meaning: Directly affects power tools and garden equipment, signaling future requirements around product disassembly, spare parts availability, and repairability scoring.
items.action: Engage engineering and supplier teams to assess product repairability and spare parts logistics.

sources.title: Fix it, don't bin it: the EU consults on Ecodesign repairability requirements

items.title: Reports Indicate European Commission May Withdraw Green Claims Directive
items.what: Media outlets report that the European Commission has abandoned plans to proceed with the proposed Green Claims Directive.
items.meaning: Although standalone green claim verification rules may be shelved, general anti-greenwashing requirements under the Empowering Consumers Directive still apply to branded products.
items.action: Ensure all consumer-facing green claims remain audited and substantiated under general EU consumer law.
